props.headline: One Distributed SQL Engine. Not a Bolt-On Stack.
props.subheadline: Most teams stitch four or more systems together long before they hit true scale — an operational database, a warehouse, a search/vector store, and sharding middleware. TiDB consolidates them onto a single distributed SQL engine: lower cost, fewer failure modes, no ETL, and AI-ready.

props.eyebrow: The Cost of the Bolt-On Stack

items.title: Every system you add is another failure mode
items.description: Every system you add is another set of licenses, another pipeline to keep in sync, another failure mode, and another migration when it hits its ceiling. ETL between them adds latency and cost, and analytics always lag production. Consolidating onto one engine removes the seams — one system to scale, secure, and operate, on fresh data.

props.title: TiDB replaces the sprawl of point systems
props.subtitle: One MySQL-compatible distributed SQL engine — elastic, strongly consistent, and built for transactional and analytical work on the same live data.

rows.ours: Native columnar HTAP with TiFlash — no ETL

items.title: TiFlash columnar replicas plus optimizer pushdown
items.description: Run OLTP and OLAP on the same fresh data, in one system — no separate warehouse, no ETL pipelines, no data lag. Transactions are strict ACID with snapshot isolation, coordinated by the Placement Driver, so consolidation never costs you consistency.

items.q: Does consolidating onto TiDB mean giving up analytics performance?
items.a: No. TiFlash keeps columnar replicas so a single query can span row and column stores on fresh data, with no ETL — you get warehouse-style analytics on live operational data.

items.q: Is TiDB a drop-in replacement for MySQL?
items.a: TiDB is binary-compatible with the MySQL 8.0 wire protocol — most applications connect with no code change. Validate specifics in a proof-of-concept with your own schema and queries.

items.q: How does TiDB replace a separate vector database?
items.a: Vector search is built into the engine, so AI and retrieval workloads run alongside your operational data — no separate store to sync or secure.

items.q: Do I need sharding middleware or caches in front of TiDB?
items.a: No manual sharding. Data auto-splits and rebalances, and strong consistency removes much of the need for a separate caching tier.

items.q: How does TiDB handle distributed transactions and ACID?
items.a: Strict ACID with snapshot-isolation transactions coordinated by the Placement Driver — strong consistency across all nodes.

items.q: How should I evaluate a consolidation move?
items.a: Run a POC on your own schema and workload — the architectural differences (MySQL wire, native HTAP, disaggregated storage, built-in vector) are structural, not benchmark tuning.
